subject.title: Feature request: config option to suppress transient tool error warnings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public normal-chat tool-error delivery policy beyond `messages.suppressToolErrors`, and what should happen when a mutating tool fails but the assistant final reply sounds successful?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the UX gap, but the next change would add public config surface and alter safety behavior around failed side effects, so automation cannot choose the product contract safely.

options.title: Add opt-in delivery enum
options.body: Define a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off` that preserves current visible warnings by default while allowing hosted/team-chat operators to opt into final-only or off behavior with focused tests.

options.title: Keep boolean-only policy
options.body: Treat `messages.suppressToolErrors` as the supported all-off escape hatch and close or defer the success-aware enum after documenting that boundary.

options.title: Move policy to channels
options.body: Let team-chat plugins own warning visibility where channel UX differs, avoiding another global message config key.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in delivery enum
recommendation.body: Define a default-compatible enum such as `all | final | off` that preserves current visible warnings by default while allowing hosted/team-chat operators to opt into final-only or off behavior with focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest inspected history on the current warning-policy path and authored the merged related PR that explicitly left this broader issue open.
